headline: Microsoft finds how to backdoor AI agents without retraining
dek: Fewer than 10 neurons are enough, per Microsoft Research.

s2.title: What happened
body: Microsoft researchers described Lazarus, a technique that plants a backdoor in an AI agent without retraining the model (Microsoft Research).

caption.hook: Microsoft showed how to plant a backdoor in an AI agent by altering fewer than ten neurons.
body: Per Microsoft Research, the Lazarus technique needs no retraining: reprogramming a few dormant neurons is enough to make the agent run malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The altered model, the company says, still passes standard safety evaluations.

The company says the risk is highest for agents with tool or terminal access, since the code runs with the agent's own access. The defense, per Microsoft, is to compare weights against an original copy, verify provenance, limit what the model can do and monitor its activity. The Foundry platform already includes some of those checks.
